reference.en:
**Вывод.** Do not enter Germany at the incumbent's €70 — the club breaks even only at €90.70, so entry is justified only if Ulmethrayne can prove a differentiation that supports that higher price.

**Факты.** First, capacity is fixed: 10 hours a day across 7 days and 15 courts gives 1,050 court-hours a week, 70% utilization gives 735, and at 3 members per hour that caps membership at 2,205. Second, €200,000 of annual cost across 2,205 members sets breakeven at €90.70 — €20.70 above the €70 the dominant player charges. Third, matching €70 would require 2,857.14 members, which is 952.38 court-hours or 90.70% utilization against a stated ceiling of 70% — physically unavailable, not merely expensive.

**Риск.** Internally, the entire 2,205 ceiling rests on one assumption — 3 members per court-hour from a 50/50 singles-doubles mix; if it is closer to 2, breakeven moves above €90.70. Externally, the incumbent holds 70% of the German market at €70 with a lower cost base, so any attempt to compete on price is a war the client cannot win.

**Next step.** Run a willingness-to-pay test at €90.70 against the €70 market price on the target urban segment before any site commitment, and validate the 3-members-per-hour mix from actual booking data.

Read it and give the launch verdict — and say explicitly whether the world-price argument in the notes changes it.

Step 2. What the grower then does with the freed acreage. Book text, p. 75: «we can assume that farmers will keep half of their land for sugar and repurpose the rest of the land for growing cabbage.»
Step 3. Market note left in the file, p. 73: a doubling of production «would cause an immediate worldwide sugar glut and rapidly falling prices».
Step 4. Inputs on hand, p. 74: «The elasticity of demand for sugar is 1». Cabbage is «one fifth as profitable as sugar».

Step 5. Side notes carried over from the file: growers in the region rotate crops on an annual cycle; cabbage is sold into local markets rather than exported; the sales team has an existing relationship with the grower cooperatives; the product is sold as an annual input, not a one-time licence.

reference.en: Launch the product: it raises grower profit per acre by 10%, and the world-price argument in the notes does not overturn that. The technology lets a grower produce the same amount of sugar on half the land, so sugar output per grower is unchanged; the freed half goes to cabbage at one fifth the profitability of sugar, giving 1 + 0.5 × (1/5) = 1.10 per acre, a 10% gain. Next: test cabbage suitability on the freed acreage across a grower sample, and confirm with the cooperatives that sugar acreage is genuinely halved rather than sugar output raised.

drills.title: Eight Hundred Storefronts
drills.prompt: A private equity fund is weighing a bid for Aubrissac, a leading French clothing retail group that has been opening stores steadily for several years. Looking at the group's own investment plan, the fund's deal team has noticed that the overall operating margin has fallen year after year over that period, and they are uneasy about it. Is the fund right to be worried? Tell them what that falling number does and does not tell us about the business.

lines: **Цель**
Фонд прямых инвестиций рассматривает покупку Aubrissac — лидера французского рынка розничной торговли одеждой. «The Client has no specific financial target or timeline.»
**Рынок**
Французский рынок одежды состоит из двух сегментов:
- Urban: «trendy, high quality, quite expensive»
- Suburban: «mass market, lower quality, low prices»
За последние 5 лет: «The market is flat in value over the last 5 years (~$25B), but volumes have been growing over the same period (~2% per year).»
**Цель сделки (актив)**
«The target has total annual sales of $800M across 800 stores. It consists of 4 brands on each of the urban and suburban market segments.»
**Экономика точки (по одному из брендов, метрика sales/sq ft)**
**Что видит команда фонда**
Фонд изучил инвестиционный план цели за последние годы. Наблюдение, которым фонд встревожен, сформулировано так: «Overall operating margin kept decreasing over the past years.»
**Условия, которые клиент подтверждает по запросу**
- «All stores are similar»
- «No cannibalization or coordination diminishing returns»
- «Opening new stores impact mainly fixed costs»
**План открытий на ближайшие годы**
«3 additional stores in year 7 and 2 additional stores in year 8.»

Числовое основание: даже внутри одного бренда книга печатает разброс площадей в 2 раза (1 600 против 800 кв. футов, стр. 192) и разброс доходности в 1,8 раза ($1 500 против $2 750 за кв. фут) — то есть однородность парка из 800 магазинов не самоочевидна.

reference.en: Build the savings product first — the deposit gap it delivers is $7 billion, and that is what has to outweigh a $200 million profit gap. On product economics checking wins: $280 per account across 1,500,000 accounts is $420,000,000 of lifetime profit against $110 across 2,000,000 accounts, or $220,000,000, for savings; the difference, $200,000,000, is what we give up, and it is a figure we build, not one the book prints. But the stated objective is lowering the cost of funds for the credit card portfolio, and on that metric savings generates $10 billion in deposits against $3 billion for checking — a $7 billion gap, again built, not printed. Since the unselected product launches the following year, we capture the checking profit one year later rather than forgo it. Risk: savings earns only $110 per account and lives 5 years against checking's 10, so the base must be re-acquired twice as often; risk: the $10 billion rests on $5,000 average balances at 2% paid to customers, and a rate move changes both the volume and its price. Next: quantify how many basis points $10 billion of deposits takes off the credit card portfolio's funding cost and test that saving against $200,000,000; and validate the $5,000 average balance assumption across 2,000,000 accounts before committing the IT build.
